howToCalculate.title: How to calculate seguro-desemprego in 2026
howToCalculate.p1: The formal-worker estimate starts with the arithmetic average of the latest available monthly salaries before dismissal.
howToCalculate.p2: The average is then applied to the 2026 MTE table: 80% in the first band, 50% of the excess plus a fixed amount in the second band, or the ceiling in the top band.

table2026.title: 2026 seguro-desemprego table
table2026.p1: This calculator uses the table effective since 2026-01-11, with a R$1,621.00 floor, bands at R$2,222.17 and R$3,703.99, a R$1,777.74 fixed amount, and a R$2,518.65 ceiling.
table2026.p2: The source is the 2026 MTE news item, accessed on 2026-06-19. The older formal MTE page still shows a 2024 table and was not used for these values.

parcelCount.title: How many payments can I receive
parcelCount.p1: The count depends on the request number and months worked in the 36 months before dismissal.
parcelCount.p2: For the first request, 12 to 23 months gives 4 payments and 24 or more gives 5. Second and later requests include ranges starting at 9 or 6 months.

eligibility.title: Who is covered by this formal-worker estimate
eligibility.p1: This estimate covers Brazilian CLT/formal workers dismissed without cause. Resignation, dismissal for cause, mutual agreement, voluntary dismissal plans, and other reasons show as not eligible from the entered data.
eligibility.p2: Indirect termination keeps the formula visible, but it needs official, judicial, or administrative recognition before entitlement is confirmed.

officialDifference.title: Why the official result may differ
officialDifference.text: MTE and gov.br use CNIS, eSocial, request history, prior used employment links, income, benefits, and administrative processing that this calculator cannot access.

requestWhen.title: When to request through gov.br or Digital Work Card
requestWhen.text: For formal workers, the usual window runs from the 7th to the 120th day after dismissal. Use the dates to detect alerts, then confirm in the official channel.

q1.question: What are the minimum and maximum seguro-desemprego amounts in 2026?
q1.answer: Under the 2026 MTE table used here, the payment is not below R$1,621.00 and not above R$2,518.65.

q2.question: Which salaries go into the average?
q2.answer: Use the latest complete monthly salaries before dismissal. The calculator uses positive values entered across the three salary fields.

q3.question: How many payments do I receive on the first, second, or later request?
q3.answer: It depends on the request number and months worked in the last 36 months; the rule may release 3, 4, or 5 payments.

q4.question: Does resignation or mutual agreement qualify?
q4.answer: For this formal-worker modality, resignation, dismissal for cause, mutual agreement, voluntary dismissal plans, and other reasons show as not eligible from the entered data.

q5.question: Can indirect termination qualify for seguro-desemprego?
q5.answer: It can be simulated financially, but the calculator marks it for official review because recognition of indirect termination is not decided here.

q6.question: Can I receive it if I have other income or an INSS benefit?
q6.answer: Sufficient own income or an incompatible continuing benefit may block the benefit. Set the declarations according to your real situation.

q7.question: Does this calculator replace gov.br?
q7.answer: No. It estimates from typed data; the official system validates records and administrative rules not available to the tool.

q8.question: Does domestic-worker seguro-desemprego use this same table?
q8.answer: Not necessarily. This first version only calculates formal/CLT workers and does not cover domestic workers, defeso insurance, or rescued workers.
